images.title: 462: one more, one less, one more
images.purpose: Shows that hundreds and units are one more than a multiple of 11 and tens one less, so 462 is a multiple of 11.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Three lines of working stacked in the centre with coloured excess and shortfall, and a total underneath.
images.exact_structure: Three rounded boxes stacked vertically and left aligned. Box 1: 400 = 396 + 4, with + 4 in green (#009E73) and the caption 4 more at its right. Box 2: 60 = 66 − 6, with − 6 in vermilion (#D55E00) and the caption 6 less at its right. Box 3: 2 = 0 + 2, with + 2 in green (#009E73). A thin dark line under the boxes, then in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) box: 4 + 2 − 6 = 0, and under it 462 = 11 × 42. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The excesses 4 and 2 cancel the shortfall 6, so 462 is a multiple of 11.

image_decisions.why: Three short lines show the alternating more and less pattern of place values on the concept's own number.
